revision: 2026-10-25 institutional sources independently reviewed; estimates grouped 25 years, no invented yearly values

primary_estimate.dataset: SlaveVoyages Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Estimates (carrier=Great Britain; cells=embarked; rows=25-year periods)
primary_estimate.definition: Estimated number of people forced to embark from Africa on vessels categorized as Great Britain carrier, NOT voyages, not arrivals, not RAC-only, not all inhabitants of British colonies.

period_rows.qualification: zero in model's carrier/period cell is not a proof that no English individual ever participated indirectly

published_subtotals.computation: 0+33695+122367+272200; all carriers 352844+315050+488065+719675; sums of DISPLAYED historical estimates rows, not new model fit
published_subtotals.warning: The displayed bins include year 1700 (and exclude year 1600). Do not reuse this sum as a precise 1600-1699 count. No year-by-year Scottish/English carrier correction reconstructed.

voyage_evidence.dataset: Smithsonian NMAAHC Royal African Company share certificate contextual history
voyage_evidence.operator: Royal African Company (English company; subset of British carrier)
voyage_evidence.transported_definition: museum states transported, not a new count of British-total embarkations
voyage_evidence.qualification: Approximate annual voyages and persons during RAC monopoly. Not additive to Great Britain SlaveVoyages totals or the Bristol 1680-92 overlapping subset.

voyage_evidence.dataset: Bristol Radical History Group, Edward Colston Research Paper #1, Tables 3 and 4
voyage_evidence.operator: Royal African Company voyages retrieved from SlaveVoyages in that study
voyage_evidence.qualification: Secondary scholarly reconstruction from historical SlaveVoyages extract. This is a specific RAC-filtered, 1680-1692 cohort; figures/analysis may vary with database version. Difference is a cohort-based transit-loss proxy, not a global 17C British mortality rate, not a count of killings by specific rebel events.

voyage_evidence.dataset: UK National Archives Royal African Company record descriptions
voyage_evidence.qualification: Catalog describes voyage summaries, individuals enslaved by the Company; no numeric voyage total extracted from archival fonds description.

coding: three or more people jumping overboard/escaping
resistance_methodology.prevalence_statement: Secondary SlaveVoyages/Slavery and Remembrance overview says roughly one in ten voyage experienced some form of African resistance. Not restricted to Great Britain, nor seventeenth century; DO NOT multiply period voyage counts by 10%.

terms: force and sale at coastal factories
plantation forced labor and racial hereditary laws
resistance at sea and in plantation societies
